subjects.subject: judge-calibration-and-drift
subjects.evidence: crates/runner/src/calibrate_watch.rs:81 alarms on a configured drift_threshold with no measured repeatability floor beneath it (crates/core/src/calibration.rs:26 Agreement carries pearson/mae/rmse/bias/kappa and no per-dimension self-agreement or good-vs-bad spread), so the sentinel cannot tell a drop from the judge arguing with itself and the golden set at crates/runner/src/calibrate.rs:2 is never split before it is used to choose a judge.

subjects.subject: cross-provider-benchmark-operations
subjects.evidence: crates/runner/src/compare.rs:773 writes the per-case result row with no concession field, while crates/engine/src/codex/mod.rs:171 announces a real handicap (an oversized system prompt folded into the user turn) only on stderr and crates/engine/src/providers.rs:222 sheds the JSON schema into a prose retry whose SchemaEnforcement::Shed never leaves the engine - so a cell measured on a weakened task renders as commensurable with the rest; entitlement exhaustion is likewise unrepresentable, crates/runner/src/compare.rs:183 reducing each cell to a bool before the breaker, so a spent allowance reports as an unhealthy provider.

subjects.subject: quality-regression-gating
subjects.evidence: crates/store/src/schema/tables/eval.rs:72 stores baseline_score as a bare Real with no judge model, dataset version or set-at date, and crates/runner/src/history.rs:6 builds the comparability predicate from mode, target and dataset version only - so the floor test at crates/runner/src/stats/paired.rs:135 compares against a number from a possibly retired instrument and can neither refuse nor date it.

subjects.subject: scoring-rubrics
subjects.evidence: crates/runner/src/rubric.rs:274 picks the weakest dimension by raw mean with min_by, ignoring RubricDimension.weight, and crates/api/src/rubrics.rs:64 validates only weight > 0 with no stated or asserted total - so the recommendation can send an operator at a light dimension while a heavier one costs more composite, and adding a dimension silently deflates every other one.
